svg.title: Evidence system for building the causal graph — overview (who writes what)
svg.desc: One person, one main agent (the orchestrator) and two subagents (literature, test). Five pipeline steps joined by files: a queue of open questions feeds extraction from papers; every claim triggers a search for corroborating and contradicting papers; claims (including those from equations) are tested blind against benchmarks and fixed causal tests, rated supported → tested → established, summarized on a card, and decided by the human. Only the human writes CONTEXT.md, PROTOCOL.md and the decisions. Decisions generate graph.yaml, tagged by regime, which the separate DAG-GP model reads but never edits.
svg.text: Building the causal graph from the literature — overview
Five pipeline steps joined by files · a paper's claim is tested in your regimes, not taken on trust · you make every call
yours: you, or a file only you write
file an agent writes — writer named on it
outside the loop · never edited by it
badge on a file = past entries are never edited · new entries only added at the end
“Yours” (human-only) = only you can change it. It is a file or a decision — never an agent.
① ROLES — one person · one main agent · two subagents
set queue order · triage papers · decide
the session you talk to · launches both subagents
runs the test bench (step 3) · never sees papers
launches each one · hands off one job at a time
② STANDING FILES — memory between sessions · read STATUS.md first · orange = only you write · blue = an agent writes (named on the box)
where we are in the chain
at once · you set the order
your signed decision is saved here
conflict → deciding experiment · no benchmark → find one

Steps are jobs, not files or agents: the badge says who does each job, IN / OUT list the files it reads and writes. OUT files are written automatically by that step — except decisions/E-xx.md, which you write.
Equations. An empirical equation becomes claims (exists · sign · lag) and goes through the same benchmarks and causal tests. No stated direction → it cannot support an edge.
Your papers. PDFs you put in papers/to-scan/ skip the triage card and go straight to extraction and testing.
④ OUTPUT — one file leaves the system
Each edge gets a verdict for each regime (early development · rapid intensification · neither),
defined in CONTEXT.md. graph.yaml tags each edge with the regimes it holds in, so
picking a regime gives you that regime's graph.
Rare regimes will return more "untestable" — that is a finding, not a failure.
script writes it from your signed decisions
Agents never supply an edge, lag, footprint, threshold, or causal conclusion. They may propose a new node, with a source, to INBOX.md — never remove one. You move accepted nodes into CONTEXT.md.
⑤ ACCESS — who can read or change each standing file (proposed)
Only you write CONTEXT.md, PROTOCOL.md and decisions/ — no pipeline agent has write access to them. That is what “yours” means.
The test agent never sees TRIED.md, STATUS.md, decisions/ or the papers. Proposed access, not yet confirmed — once you agree, it goes into PROTOCOL.md as the agents' rules.
⑥ QUICK REFERENCE — who writes each file · who does each step
Orchestrator adds items · you set the order
Literature agent adds candidates · you approve
The orchestrator (main agent) is not a step — it launches the subagents and keeps the files above.
